title: The limit law of the maximum of discrete partial-sums distribution II
summary: Let $X_1,\,X_2,\,\ldots,\,X_N$, $N\in\mathbb N$ be independent, discrete, integer-valued random variables. Assume that $X_j\geqslant m_j$ almost surely for each $j=1,\,2,\,\ldots,\,N$, where $m_1,\,m_2,\,\ldots,\,m_N\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $m_1+\cdots+m_N<0$. Furthermore, suppose that the sequence $X_1,\,X_2,\,\ldots$ is periodic in distribution, i.e. $X_k{\buildrel d \over =} X_{k+N}$ for all $k\in\mathbb N$. We derive computable representations for the distribution functions of $\max\{X_1,\,X_1+X_2,\,\ldots\}$, $\max\{X_2,\,X_2+X_3,\,\ldots\}$, $\ldots$,…
